title: A Radio Segment on Weekend Digital Detox
script: Radio Host: [warmly] Good morning, listeners! Today we are talking about weekend digital detox. We have a caller on the line. Hello!
Caller: Hello! Thank you for taking my call this morning.
Radio Host: [curious] Of course! Tell us, what made you decide to try a digital detox weekend?
Caller: Honestly, I noticed I was spending Saturdays just scrolling, and Sunday nights, I felt like the weekend never happened.
Radio Host: [honestly] So what exactly did you change? Did you delete every app completely?
Caller: Not that extreme. I plan offline hours once a month, while allowing urgent calls from trusted family and checking any work duty first.
Radio Host: [carefully] A whole day and a half? That sounds difficult for a lot of people, myself included.
Caller: The first time, it was genuinely uncomfortable. I kept reaching for my pocket, out of pure habit.
Radio Host: [thoughtful] What did you do instead, with all that extra time?
Caller: I read an actual book, cooked a full meal slowly, and visited my parents without checking messages the whole time.
Radio Host: [practically] Did your family notice anything different about you that weekend?
Caller: Yes, actually. My mother said I listened better than usual, without glancing at my phone every few minutes.
Radio Host: [reflective] That's a powerful observation. What changed for you personally, after doing this a few times?
Caller: I started noticing how tired scrolling actually makes me, even though it feels relaxing while I'm doing it.
Radio Host: [encouraging] Would you recommend this to other listeners, even people with busy work schedules?
Caller: A few planned hours may help. Keep emergency contact available and choose a time that does not ignore family or work duties.
Radio Host: Thank you so much for sharing this with us this morning. It's a wonderful reminder for all of us.
Caller: [warmly] Thank you for listening. I hope someone tries it this weekend, even for just a few hours.
